description: Table 2 rendered as an image: a single rectangular composition table titled "Chemical content of experimental steel (mass percentage, %)". It has eleven column headers reading No., C, Si, Mn, Al, N, P, S, O, Ti, Fe, separated from the data by a horizontal rule, and three data rows labelled 1 #, 2 # and 3 #. Row 1 #: C 0.41, Si 0.32, Mn 14.85, Al 0.868, N 0.0032, P 0.043, S 0.014, O 0.0005, Ti 0.0057, Fe Bal. Row 2 #: C 0.41, Si 0.32, Mn 14.86, Al 2.766, N 0.0029, P 0.045, S 0.014, O 0.0005, Ti 0.0059, Fe Bal. Row 3 #: C 0.41, Si 0.31, Mn 14.83, Al 4.695, N 0.0021, P 0.045, S 0.016, O 0.0013, Ti 0.0060, Fe Bal. The table therefore defines the three experimental Fe-15Mn-Al-C low-density steels whose inclusions are studied elsewhere in the paper. Across the rows C (0.41), Mn (~14.8), P, S and Ti are essentially constant, while Al is deliberately stepped up (0.868 → 2.766 → 4.695 %); N decreases and O increases as Al rises. No plots, micrographs or error bars are present — the figure's sole content is numeric composition data.

subfigures.description: Composition table with headers No., C, Si, Mn, Al, N, P, S, O, Ti, Fe and three rows for steels 1 #, 2 #, 3 #, in mass percentage; Fe reported as Bal.

observations.observation: The table headers read No., C, Si, Mn, Al, N, P, S, O, Ti, Fe, and Fe is given as Bal. for all three steels.
The table is stated in mass percentage (%).
The three experimental steels were named by their Al content: 1 # (Al = 0.868 %), 2 # (Al = 2.766 %) and 3 # (Al = 4.695 %).

The citing text states that the N content decreases with increasing Al content, while the O content slightly increases with increasing Al content; the table values are consistent with this (N 0.0032 → 0.0029 → 0.0021 %; O 0.0005 → 0.0005 → 0.0013 %).
The citing text states Si ≈ 0.32 % and Ti ≈ 60 ppm; the table lists Si between 0.31 and 0.32 % and Ti between 0.0057 and 0.0060 % (57-60 ppm).
C is identical (0.41 %) and Mn nearly identical (14.83-14.86 %) in all three steels, so Al is the only deliberately varied major element.
P ranges 0.043-0.045 % and S ranges 0.014-0.016 % across the three steels.
